contexts.text: There is no life dissociated from the life of others...
Delights communicated to others by transmissions.
Long for nothing more than to transfer their happiness into others.

He who has formed an opinion of his own excellence above others, is at last imbued with such a habit, and as it were nature, that wherever he goes, and looks at others, while he is speaking to them, he is attending to himself... This men can see in others.
Such a lot awaits those who suppose themselves to be greater than others.
A certain one (had) seemed to himself great and wise above others; in other respects he was upright...
In those states... He spoke with Jehovah as with another.
The Lord was born like another man.
Those who... had delighted to make the life of others delightful...
In proportion as the Lord was in the human... He adored Jehovah as one different from Himself. AC 2159:3.
(Thus) the Lord was not another than the Father, although He spoke about the Father as about another...
They prefer themselves before others; thus pay attention to themselves, and not to others, except in so far as they are of service to them.
For he who loves himself despises, vituperates, or hates all others who do not serve, honour, or favour him.
Because the Lord was born as another man, and in external form was like another.
The life of charity is to think well about another, and to will well to him; and to perceive joy in one's self from the fact that others also are saved...
Such is the temptation of the infants, to accustom them... not to think, speak, and act from another... HH 343:end.
That they may not boast before others...
In the love of self there is contempt of others...
In proportion as there was of the maternal human, there was another.

The spiritual... when he has done anything good, if he can mention it, and thus set himself above others, is in the delight of his life. But the celestial love the neighbour more than themselves... and never set themselves in any way above others.
Adulterers laugh at the miseries of others.
(Everyone must) will and think... from others; and these others... again from others; and so on...
To wash the feet... meant not to reflect on the evils of another; and also... to cleanse another from evils.
They did not fear that others should know their ends and intentions...

To love self above others; to will better to self than to others; to desire what belongs to another; and to study for self alone, and not for others except for the sake of self, he calls goods and also truths, because, from himself, he desires these things.
He cannot be in any heavenly Society, in which everyone wills better for others than for self.
Such Knowledges are insinuated into him as are not quite contrary... as that self must be studied first, and afterwards others.
These things man can explore with himself; but not with others...
For man receives from others only so much as he has of his Own, or else acquires for himself by the view of the Thing in himself...
Good from proprium must have regard to... the setting of self above others, consequently to contempt for others.
The natural man seems to himself to have life, when he is exalted to... supereminence above others... and is in his bliss, when he is opulent above others.
Before regeneration, he is possessed... by infernals, however he may appear to himself to be like another...
Merit... conjoins with... the thought of the pre-eminence of self above others; consequently with contempt for others. AC 4943.
Nothing can subsist from itself, but from something else; and this again from something else...
Believe themselves to be wise above others.
It is merely that he is thus instructed by others.
Man receives evils from others without his own fault.
The works they have done for others for the sake of self...
Had sought... to subjugate the minds of others.
(All) think, speak, and act... from others; and these others... from others again... AC 5986:2. AC 6470. DP 287-294.
When they... hear that heavenly blessedness is to do good to others from good will...
In the other life (such) are in the perpetual endeavour to destroy others.
Many of these Spirits are such, that they observe the faults and blemishes of others, and tell them...
When he found that... those are in the first rank who had not set themselves above others... he was indignant.
Such Spirits eagerly receive truths... that they may glory in appearing more intelligent than others.
Had lived to the world... but had not... set themselves above others...
Lot of those who have despised others...
Loves others only so far as he has regard to hem in himself...

The reason he seems to believe... is that he has faith in others, and has confirmed in himself what he has received from others. To confirm the things which are from others... is very easy... AC 5937:2.
Such never condemn others...
In order to dominate... they excite enmities, hatreds, and combats among others.
Feels delight in doing good to others.
Render themselves happy, but not others... and do not transmit the influx of happiness to others.
Had done nothing of good to others...
Such do good works for themselves, and not for others.
If they see others more blessed... they are sad.
Heavenly blessedness consists... not in being served by others; but in wanting to serve others.
Such have faith in others.
Have devised many arts in order to elevate themselves above others.
In proportion as anyone loves himself, he hates others who do not favour.
Whereas those who do not want others to know what they speak, judge concerning others, and think evil about them...
The Hells... are in the continual cupidity of doing evil to others...
If raised to honours, they do not regard themselves as more worthy than others.
They inflict evil... so far as they can through others... AC 8622:end.
Here, truths received from another are treated of.
Truths not conjoined are those learned from others...
When anyone thinks or speaks from another, the truths with him are disturbed...
The good of love is such, that what is in it is also in others from it... for it is proper to love to will that all its own be from itself in others.
Such see nothing but what they have of others...

They who have Heaven in them... perceive delight in benefiting others... But they who have Hell in them... perceive delight in doing evil to others, and if they perceive delight in benefiting them, it... is for the sake of self and the world.
They who think first from others, and make [the things they thus receive] of their faith, and view them with their own understanding afterwards, can with difficulty recede from them...
Spurious intelligence and wisdom is... to believe... what is said by others...
Heaven consists in willing from the heart better for others than for ourselves; and in serving others for the sake of their happiness...
He who wills good for himself alone is delighted at the evils which happen to others... for he wants to get for himself the goods of all others...

He who dominates from love towards the neighbour... loves nothing more than uses; thus to serve others. By serving others is meant to will good and perform uses to others, whether it be to the Church, our country, society, or our fellow-citizen...
They think that it is true, because another has said so.
That the Divine love and the Divine wisdom cannot but be and come forth in others... General article.

The essential of love is... to love others, and to be conjoined with them through love... and is also to be loved by others... Love consists in this: that what is one's own be another's... To feel one's own delight in another, and not his in one's self, is not to love... To love one's self in another, disjoins... (for) in proportion as anyone has loved another in this way, he afterwards hates him.
They regard others as if they were images.
(For) no one can regard another except from what is his own in him. He who loves another regards him from his own love in him; and he who is wise regards another from his own wisdom in him...
It is the like with the Divine, (which) cannot regard itself from another...
(Such) explore with others nothing else than their cupidities and desires, and thus lead them...
One Spirit can infuse his thoughts and affections into another... This is called thinking from another, and thinking in another.
Servants = those who are in such things from others; thus from the memory.
It is inscribed on the wisdom of the wise, that no one is wise, or lives, for himself alone, unless at the same time for others... To live for others is to do uses.
Man becomes a hypocrite when he thinks much about himself, and sets himself above others. (Explained.)
Man is not born for the sake of himself, but for the sake of others; that is, that he should not live for himself alone, but for others...
(On those who seek solicitously for evil in others.)
(On those who suppose things to have been done by themselves which were really done by others.)
a. (On those who can scarcely think anything good of others.)
Some Spirits always appears in the persons of others. Explained.
If they could, they would never leave anything of delight for others.
On the sphere of those who esteem others as nothing. SE 2684.
On those who do not despise others, but still hold them as of little account...
On the sphere of those who... desire to command others.
On those who induce others to believe whatever they propose.
That impressions about others are eradicated there with extreme difficulty.
They want to derive their phantasy to others, and thus draw others into punishment, and so substitute others in their place.
On those who within themselves condemn others, but speak differently.
The punishment of those who deceitfully attribute their own evils to others.
They then begin to speak evilly of others, and well of themselves.
They are such as in the world draw out the interior thoughts of others...
On those who do nothing from themselves, but from others.
When anyone supposes himself to be greater than others...
This is done by entering into the minds of others...
When the celestial hear truths from others, they see them...
On those who can say sharp things against others, so that they cannot answer.
How the Societies of friendship draw away delights from others.
On those who know only from others.
For to believe what another says is slavery.
To see from others is only to know.
It is believed to be so, because another has said it. AE 401:35. AE 427:4.
To see these things from another is not intelligence, but knowledge.
Historical faith must precede, which is the Knowledge of the things of the Church and of Heaven from others.
Most of them are in faith from others; but still are in life according to faith.
Servants = those who think from others.
The understanding and will do not act a one when the man is with others.
